assumptions: critical_swimming_speed_m_s=0.4: about 11 body lengths/s, mid-range for adult zebrafish (0.3-0.5 m/s).
current_speed_m_s=0.2: 50% of Ucrit, a generous margin below it.
bladder_volume_at_depth_ml=0.02332: 0.024/1.029, from Boyle's law at 0.3 m.
powered=false and flight_mode='glide': two explicit no-flight declarations, as the brief requires.
intake_J_per_day=93.75: chosen so intake*assimilation = 75 J/d, which balances routine+activity with mass_change 0.
routine_cost_J_per_day=55: ~0.2 mg O2/g/h x 0.8 g x 24 h x ~14 J/mg, rounded.
reference_sustained_power_W=0.00023625: 0.0002 / 2.3^-0.2, so the 26 C value is 0.84657 times the 28 C reference.
notes: I did not run lean_check, so no value has been checked against the laws. No law blocks the brief. Agent 0 proposed flight_mode 'none'; I used 'glide' because it is the value the brief names. Agent 1 left out the bladder keys; I kept Agent 0's pair, which agrees with Boyle's law. Agent 2 supplied cardiacOutput, arterialO2, o2_store_ml, oxycaloric and efficiency with units it could not verify. I dropped them because a unit mismatch could create a false violation, and they only feed the aerobic-demand laws that powered=false already takes out of scope. The cost is that any other law reading them returns cannot-evaluate. Flight numeric keys and the drag keys are omitted, so those laws are cannot-evaluate or out-of-scope rather than violated.
